edges.target: Persistent Outer Nuclear Layer Thinning and Visual Field Defect

nodes.description: Deep capillary plexus ischemia infarcts the outer plexiform layer (OPL) and outer nuclear layer (ONL), producing acute hyperreflectivity at the OPL/ONL junction on OCT that enlarges over the first week, with disruption of the ellipsoid zone and outer segment/RPE junction. The lesion is best visualized as a dark area on near-infrared reflectance imaging.

evidence.reference_title: Acute macular neuroretinopathy: long-term insights revealed by multimodal imaging.
evidence.snippet: Two patients were seen within the first 1 to 2 days of symptoms, and both showed outer nuclear and outer plexiform layer hyperreflectivity.

evidence.reference_title: The characteristics of acute macular neuroretinopathy following COVID-19 infection.
evidence.snippet: hyperreflective lesions at the level of the outer plexiform layer (OPL) and outer nuclear layer (ONL) and disruption of the ellipsoid zone (EZ) on spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) B-scans

nodes.description: Lesions wider than 100 micrometers develop persistent thinning of the outer nuclear layer that correlates with long-term visual field deficits (paracentral scotomas). Visual acuity often recovers within weeks, but scotomas frequently persist for months or longer.
nodes.id: Persistent Outer Nuclear Layer Thinning and Visual Field Defect

evidence.reference_title: Acute macular neuroretinopathy: long-term insights revealed by multimodal imaging.
evidence.snippet: Thinning of the outer nuclear layer persisted in all patients with lesions >100 μm width, and in one patient this thinning worsened over the course of follow-up

evidence.reference_title: The characteristics of acute macular neuroretinopathy following COVID-19 infection.
evidence.snippet: all patients achieved a BCVA of 20/40 or better, but 9 patients (81.8%) continued to experience persistent scotomas

nodes.description: In predisposed individuals, transient microvascular occlusion/ischemia develops in the deep capillary plexus (DCP) of the retina, the vascular bed supplying the outer plexiform and outer nuclear layers. OCT angiography directly demonstrates a flow void in the DCP co-localized with the acute lesion, with partial recovery of flow signal on follow-up in most cases.

evidence.reference_title: OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY ANGIOGRAPHY OF ACUTE MACULAR NEURORETINOPATHY REVEALS DEEP CAPILLARY ISCHEMIA.
evidence.snippet: Optical coherence tomography angiography illustrated a flow void in the deep retinal capillary plexus associated with the AMN lesion.

evidence.reference_title: Projection-Resolved OCT Angiography of Microvascular Changes in Paracentral Acute Middle Maculopathy and Acute Macular Neuroretinopathy.
evidence.snippet: All five eyes had reduced DCP flow signal, along with normal SCP, MCP, and choriocapillaris flow signal in the area of the lesion
